column3: Repeat UAV Lidar Surveys Following the 2025 Eaton Fire
column4: The data consist of repeated UAV lidar surveys collected after the Eaton Fire across 14 debris basins and five Bailey catchments between January and March 2025. Supporting data include airborne lidar, rainfall records, fixed-camera photographs, debris-basin capacities and excavation records, and USGS debris-flow volume predictions.

column3: Hillslope hydrological monitoring data in Puerto Rico, October 2021 to September 2025
column4:
Time-series data from 18 hillslope hydrologic monitoring stations installed in Puerto Rico following Hurricane María (2017). Their primary scientific focus is to investigate subsurface hydrologic response to rainfall and develop a quantitative link between rainfall, soil moisture, and landsliding. This datasets contains soil volumetric water content at four depth intervals of 25 cm, soil water potential, and pore-water pressure, all logged at 5-minute intervals. 

For more information, please visit the official USGS data release: https://www.usgs.gov/data/hillslope-hydrological-monitoring-data-puerto-rico-october-2021-september-2025
